_note: File-transport example (the default). For the `command` transport (pipe to any LLM CLI) and other setups, see examples/ and docs/INTEGRATIONS.md. Every optional field below shows its default; delete any you don't need.
_securityNote: broca-machina fails closed: it refuses to start unless you either set discord.allowedUserId (recommended — only that user's speech is transcribed) OR set discord.allowAnySpeaker:true to explicitly accept ANY speaker in the channel. Accepted speech reaches your brain directly; with a command/mcp brain (an LLM/agent), every accepted speaker inherits the brain's privileges, so treat transcripts as untrusted (prompt injection). Keep allowedUserId set for any agent brain.
_sttModelNote: WHISPER_MODEL is the STT speed/accuracy lever. Default small.en (most accurate on CPU). Set it to base.en for ~2.8x faster transcription with near-identical output on short utterances, or tiny.en for fastest/roughest — one env var, default unchanged. The warm stt_server.py reads it too (warm-servers.sh injects stt.env), so switch it here and restart the warm servers.
_mcpTransportNote: For transport.type 'mcp' (the loop IS an MCP server; see docs/INTEGRATIONS.md): transcriptDir (optional) tees every transcript to a file so an external router can forward it; gateFile (optional) suppresses the MCP channel notification while that file exists (a router owns delivery, and the ack stays armed); replyFile (optional) is polled as an additional voice source — whatever writes it is spoken. All three default to off.
_presenceGating: autoJoin=false (default) keeps the bot in the channel for the whole session. Set autoJoin=true for presence-gated behavior: the gateway stays connected but the bot only JOINS the voice channel while allowedUserId is in it (or, with allowAnySpeaker, while any non-bot member is), and LEAVES idleLeaveMs after they go (a quick rejoin cancels the leave). onPresenceEnter/onPresenceLeave run a command (detached) on those edges — e.g. warm/spin-down the STT/TTS servers so model load overlaps the join. presenceFile (optional) is kept in existence exactly while that user is in the channel, so external tooling can gate on presence without polling Discord.
_vadNote: Silero-VAD endpointing (opt-in). enabled=false (default) keeps the fixed endSilenceMs trailing-silence endpointing. enabled=true streams decoded PCM to the warm vad_server.py (start it with `warm-servers.sh start vad`, or add VOICE_WARM_VAD=1 to onPresenceEnter.env so `start` includes it) and ends the utterance the instant speech stops — typically several hundred ms sooner than the fixed timeout, without shortening endSilenceMs (which stays the fallback if the VAD server is down/unreachable). threshold/minSilenceMs/minSpeechMs are live-tunable; the defaults below are conservative starting points and want a live voice test to dial in.
_ttsPipelineNote: Sentence-boundary TTS pipelining (opt-in). false (default) synthesizes the whole reply then plays it. true splits long replies at sentence boundaries and synthesizes chunk N+1 while chunk N plays, cutting time-to-first-audio on long replies. Only replies >= minChars are pipelined; chunks are merged up to maxChunkChars. Preserves ordering and barge-in.
_bargeConfirmNote: Confirm-before-kill barge-in (default true when bargeIn is on). A speaking-start during bot playback DUCKS the audio to 30% and lets STT decide: real speech interrupts playback and drops any queued reply tail (classic barge-in), while a noise blob — breath, mic bump, the bot's own audio leaking into an open mic — just restores the volume, so phantom 'utterances' can no longer cut long replies off mid-sentence. Set false for the classic instant interrupt.
_earconNote: Thinking earcon (opt-in, default off). After the turn's ack, if the reply STILL hasn't landed afterMs later, a quiet ambient loop (assets/thinking.wav ships as a soft pulse; any wav works) plays at `volume` until the reply, a new utterance, or barge-in cuts it — non-verbal 'still working' for long agent-brain waits without more spoken filler.
_ackNote: Fast acknowledgement (perceived latency). ackAfterMs=0 (default) is off. Set it >0 to speak an ack phrase that many ms AFTER you stop talking IF the brain's real reply hasn't landed yet — a quick 'still thinking' filler that overlaps STT + brain time so a slow (LLM/agent) brain doesn't leave the channel silent. ackPhrase is a string or an array: with an array the filler rotates randomly (never the same one twice in a row) so it doesn't chant one phrase every turn. All phrases are pre-rendered at startup so firing one is instant, it works for every transport, and a fast reply preempts it (no double-talk). Good value ~600 for a slow brain; leave 0 for a fast echo/command brain.
_addressGateNote: Address gate (opt-in): filters out speech the enrolled speaker directs at OTHER people in the room. A wake word anywhere in the utterance delivers instantly; every other utterance is judged ADDRESSED/ASIDE by a warm local Ollama model (defaults borrowed from localAck) given the recent conversation as context. Asides are logged and teed to transcriptDir with an .aside suffix — never forwarded to the brain, never firing a filler. FAIL-OPEN: any judge error or timeout delivers normally. Cost: ~judge latency (0.5-1s) before delivery on wake-word-less turns.
_semanticEndpointNote: Semantic endpointing (default ON). Endpointers cut at silence, but a pause is not always the end of a thought: a transcript that sounds unfinished (trailing comma, dangling connective like 'the/and/because' — read from Whisper's own punctuation) is HELD for holdMs instead of delivered; a continuation spoken inside the window is joined into one turn, none coming it flushes as-is. Lets you keep FAST silence endpointing (low turn latency) without mid-thought cutoffs — a wrong hold costs holdMs on that turn, a wrong cut costs nothing new. Set enabled:false for strict every-pause-is-a-turn behavior.
_speakerGateNote: Speaker verification (opt-in): respond only to ONE enrolled voice. refFile is the voiceprint (JSON centroid built by src/speaker.py; embedding model: sherpa-onnx, pip install sherpa-onnx + download a speaker model to ~/.cache/broca-machina/speaker/). With refFile configured but ABSENT, the loop runs a short spoken enrollment conversation on join (enrollUtterances samples; nothing said during enrollment reaches your brain), builds the voiceprint, then arms. ENFORCEMENT lives in the STT layer: set VOICE_SPEAKER_REF (and optionally VOICE_SPEAKER_THRESHOLD, default 0.5 — start LOW, e.g. 0.35, and tune UP from the scores stt logs, or your own voice may be rejected) in stt.env below. Rejected utterances transcribe to empty and are handled like phantoms. PRIVACY: samples + voiceprint are biometric data — keep refFile/enrollDir outside the repository (e.g. ~/.cache/broca-machina/speaker/). To re-enroll, delete refFile and rejoin.
